transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, what finally made me come in is that my appetite has just been all over the place for months now. I have these stretches where I just skip dinner entirely and end up losing weight without even trying to. And then... on other nights, I'll just sit and pick at crackers or a bowl of cereal, mostly because the thought of actually cooking a meal for myself just feels completely pointless.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I'm not really sure. I... I haven't noticed feeling sad, if that's what you mean. I wouldn't necessarily say I feel depressed, exactly. It's just... like I said, things just feel a bit pointless lately.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Not really. I mean, I still go through the motions of the things I used to love doing. Like, I'll go out to water the garden, or I'll show up to my book club... but most of the time, it just feels flat. I don't really get any joy out of it anymore, so I usually end up leaving early, or sometimes I just don't even bother starting.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time this started?
Well, yes. This has all been going on since my divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago now.
Have these symptoms been present continuously for more than six months?

Yes, it has. Like I just mentioned, it really started right around when the divorce was finalized... so it's been a solid year and seven months of feeling this way. It hasn't really let up since then, so yes, definitely longer than six months.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Well, yes. I want to be clear that I don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself, but... I do sometimes catch myself thinking that it would just be a relief not to wake up. Honestly, it scares me when my mind goes there, because I know I would take it very seriously if one of my clients said that to me. So, yes, I have been having those thoughts.
Since this began, have there been any stretches of at least two months when you felt mostly back to your usual self?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it really hasn't let up. I mean, I might have a day or two where things feel a little easier to manage, but... no, definitely not a stretch of two months where I felt back to my usual self. It's been pretty much a constant weight this whole time.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

Yes, I have. It's actually been pretty tough. Even on days when my caseload isn't unusually heavy, I just feel like I'm dragging my body through the hospital. It takes so much effort just to get through the shift. And then when I finally get home, I'm just... I'm too tired to do much of anything. I don't have the energy to cook, or do my stretches, or even answer personal messages from friends. I'm just completely drained.
Before this started after your divorce, had you ever gone through another period lasting at least a couple of weeks where you felt this same kind of loss of interest or low mood?
No, I really haven't. I mean, I've had stressful times before, of course, but... nothing like this. This is the first time I've ever felt this way for this long.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes, I really have. Um, especially at work. When I'm doing case reviews, I find myself having to reread the same notes several times because the information just isn't sinking in. And making decisions has gotten strangely difficult. Just simple things, like figuring out which client call to return first, or... or even what to buy for dinner. It can take me an embarrassing amount of time just to figure it out.
Have you been feeling worthless, or blaming yourself a lot?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep replaying the marriage in my head. I keep telling myself that I must have failed at something really basic for it to end this way. I mean, part of me knows that relationships are a lot more complicated than that, but... it's just hard not to blame myself right now.
Have you ever had a period when you felt abnormally energetic or unusually up, almost like you needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I haven't. I've never had anything like that. I usually need my full eight hours of sleep to function, and I can't think of a time when I felt unusually energetic or... or "up," as you said. It's really just been this low feeling lately.
